topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The opening introduces the lecture's scope on cancer evolution and outlines the key learning objectives.

topics.label: Mutational and epigenetic mechanisms of clonal evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer clones evolve and gain competitive fitness through both genetic mutations and epigenetic modifications.

topics.label: Stem cell hierarchy and cell of origin in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the relationship between normal tissue hierarchies, cancer stem cells, and the cellular origin of malignancy in hematological and solid tumors.

topics.label: Microenvironmental influences, inflammation, and stromal dependency
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how environmental promotion, inflammatory signaling, and non-cancer stromal cells enable tumor growth and create therapeutic opportunities.

topics.label: Technologies for investigating tumor evolution and plasticity
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the genomic, transcriptomic, and spatial technologies used to analyze tumor cell heterogeneity and microenvironmental interactions in the laboratory.

topics.label: Integrated evolutionary model of tumorigenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesises how mutational succession, cell-of-origin properties, transcriptional plasticity, and microenvironmental factors converge to drive malignant progression.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next session preview
topics.groupedBecause: The closing marks the end of the lecture and previews the upcoming session on cancer therapies.
